changes.before: H&E is the purple and pink stain on almost every pathology slide: haematoxylin colours cell nuclei blue-purple and eosin colours the cytoplasm and connective tissue pink.
changes.after: H&E staining makes nuclei blue-purple and broadly colours cytoplasm and supporting tissue pink, helping show cells in their tissue setting.
changes.reason: Replace the unsupported almost-every-slide quantifier with the source-verified staining/morphology definition.

changes.before: Histopathology means looking at cancer cells under a microscope, and immunohistochemistry stains them for specific proteins. Together they are still the foundation of every diagnosis.
changes.after: Histopathology examines tissue under a microscope. Immunohistochemistry uses antibodies to show selected antigens; both need specimen context and appropriate interpretation.
changes.reason: Remove the every-diagnosis universal and distinguish tissue examination from antibody detection.

changes.before: TPS is the share of tumour cells whose membrane stains for PD-L1, ignoring immune cells. In lung cancer it decides whether pembrolizumab or cemiplimab can be given alone: 1 percent opens the door, 50 percent is where single-agent treatment is strongest.
changes.after: The tumour proportion score is the percentage of eligible viable tumour cells with qualifying PD-L1 membrane staining. Immune cells are excluded; the assay and clinical setting determine its use.
changes.reason: Define the measurement rather than presenting a short numeric treatment gate or an unverified strongest-treatment ranking. Detailed existing clinical fields remain unchanged.

changes.before: The tumour proportion score is the percentage of viable tumour cells showing partial or complete membrane staining at any intensity, read on the 22C3 pharmDx (and, for cemiplimab, also the SP263 assay). Pembrolizumab's US label uses TPS >= 1 percent for first-line single-agent treatment of stage III or metastatic NSCLC without EGFR or ALK alterations and for second-line treatment after platinum chemotherapy; cemiplimab's single-agent first-line indication requires TPS >= 50 percent. The KEYNOTE-024 trial that set the 50 percent bar and KEYNOTE-042 that lowered the gate to 1 percent are the sources of the two numbers. TPS is a lung-specific read; the same slide scored as CPS would include immune cells and give a different number.
changes.after: The tumour proportion score is the percentage of viable tumour cells showing partial or complete membrane staining at any intensity, read on the 22C3 pharmDx (and, for cemiplimab, also the SP263 assay). Pembrolizumab's US label uses TPS >= 1 percent for first-line single-agent treatment of stage III or metastatic NSCLC without EGFR or ALK alterations and for second-line treatment after platinum chemotherapy; cemiplimab's single-agent first-line indication requires TPS >= 50 percent. The KEYNOTE-024 trial that set the 50 percent bar and KEYNOTE-042 that lowered the gate to 1 percent are the sources of the two numbers. These clinical examples concern lung cancer. TPS and CPS use different eligible cell populations and can give different values; a score in another assay or cancer needs its own scoring and clinical context.
changes.reason: Correct lung-specific exclusivity and the guaranteed numerical-difference claim. The preceding clinical sentences are preserved exactly at their previous source depth.
